newsitem.title: USA: US debt fund managers trim cash allocations-survey.
newsitem.headline: US debt fund managers trim cash allocations-survey.

text.p: Money managers slightly reduced their cash allocations and modestly extended duration exposure in their U.S. debt portfolios, according to a survey by Stone & McCarthy Research Associates.
"Survey participants again extended portfolio durations slightly this week, back to near basically flat, while cash levels dipped slightly," the report said.
In the week ended July 8, the cash/assets ratio fell to 7.62 percent from 7.94 percent on an arithmetic basis and fell to 6.03 percent from 6.10 percent on a weighted basis.
The survey's actual/target duration index rose to 99.94 percent from 99.76 percent on an arithmetic basis and rose to 99.26 percent from 98.97 percent on a weighted basis.
Duration refers to a portfolio's average maturity and is used by portfolio managers to calculate exposure to risk.
The survey's bear/bull index fell to 4.83 from 4.87 on an arithmetic basis. It inched up to 4.62 from 4.59 on an asset-weighted basis.
A number above 5.00 is seen as indicating investors are mostly long on the market.
Thirteen percent of the portfolio managers surveyed said they were planning to be active in the coming week, up from 4.0 percent in the week ending July 1.
The Stone & McCarthy survey is conducted by the research firm weekly. It includes 25 market participants with total assets of about $100 billion, the firm said.
* Table provided by Stone and McCarthy Research Associates.
** Respondents intending to adjust portfolio in coming week.
